plan.purpose: Help a traveler see what the trip will cost, then follow a clear day-by-day plan with the practical advice needed to make it work.
plan.title: Your trip, day by day
plan.composition: Use the full result width as a calm, compact travel notebook: a result-led header, one full-width cost breakdown, then paired day cards in chronological reading order, followed by practical notes. The header's sole h1 reads /result/title rather than the planning title; its muted description reads /result/overview, and its action area belongs to the host. The itinerary is a two-column Grid on wide screens and a single column on narrow screens; each untitled Card has a date eyebrow, a prominent day title in Text, and a compact sequence of labelled activities. Keep every day and the practical notes open, use only h1 and h2 headings, and use theme-aware surfaces, readable text and subtle borders rather than decorative imagery. Do not add request details, a sidebar, navigation, a footer or a run control.

regions.purpose: Name the generated trip and introduce its character without repeating the host's request summary.
elements: ResultHeader: title reads /result/title with $state; description reads /result/overview with $state; eyebrow "Your itinerary"; sole h1; reserve its action area for the host's download and share actions.

regions.purpose: Put the estimated cost first and show where the money goes without duplicating the total.
elements: ProportionBar: label "Estimated trip cost"; total reads /result/estimated_total with $state; items reads /result/costs with $state; labelKey "category"; valueKey "amount"; unit reads /result/currency with $state; no ceiling. Category values remain exactly "stay", "food", "tickets", "transport", "buffer". Show the currency beside the total and category amounts; use distinct theme-safe part colors and the labelled legend.

regions.title: Day by day
regions.purpose: Make the ordered itinerary easy to scan and read, with each day's activities together and empty periods omitted.
elements: Section: h2 "Day by day"; holds the itinerary Grid.
Grid: two equal columns on wide screens, one on narrow screens; repeat /result/days read with $state in list order, left to right then downward; one untitled Card per item.
Card: holds a vertical Stack containing DateText, Text and four Detail lines; equal padding and top alignment, no nested cards.
DateText: value reads relative item path day with $item; format "weekday"; tone accent.
Text: reads relative item path title with $item; prominent semibold text, not another heading.
Detail: label "Morning"; value reads relative item path morning with $item; hide when empty.
Detail: label "Lunch"; value reads relative item path midday with $item; hide when empty.
Detail: label "Afternoon"; value reads relative item path afternoon with $item; hide when empty.
Detail: label "Evening"; value reads relative item path evening with $item; hide when empty.

regions.title: Before you go
regions.purpose: Finish with the practical advice that helps the traveler prepare and get around comfortably.
elements: Section: h2 "Before you go"; holds TextList; separated from the itinerary by a hairline.
TextList: items reads /result/practical_notes with $state; dot markers; preserve list order and show each note once.

brief:
# Result page: trip_planner.plan_trip

Plan the trip day by day, within the budget

## Frame

This page is the result page of an app that is composed, then shows its result: what the person sees after one run. The host draws what surrounds it: the band with the team's logo and the app's name, then a bar restating the request with a way back to edit it and to run again. The host also owns the actions on the result, such as downloading or sharing it, and places them where the page's header puts them. There is no side panel, no app bar and no footer to build, and nothing restates the request.

The page is the result across the full width. It opens on its header, which names the result in a person's words, read from the result itself where it can be (the page's h1). Then the figure or the fact a person looks for first, then the body of the result in the shape it naturally has: a plan day by day, options side by side to compare, a record's details. Lay out what a person reads; leave out what only a machine would.

Show each value once: a figure a component already states, such as the total inside a ProportionBar, is not repeated beside it. When the result carries the request back - the same facts the person entered, such as the topic or the tone they chose - leave that part out: the host's bar already restates the request. Write a value as a person reads it: a date in words, an amount beside its currency when the result has one.

## State

The host loads the run's result under `/result` before the page renders. Read every value with `$state`; emit no `/state` patches. Paths:

- `/result` — structure trip_planner.Itinerary: A day-by-day plan for a trip, with its estimated cost
  - `/result/title` — text — `title`: The trip's name
  - `/result/overview` — text — `overview`: The plan in two or three sentences
  - `/result/days` — list of structure trip_planner.DayPlan — `days`: The plan for each day, in order
    - each item is a structure trip_planner.DayPlan (One day of the trip), with these members (paths relative to one item, for DataTable columns or $item):
      - `day` — date — `day`: The day
      - `title` — text — `title`: What the day is about, in a few words
      - `morning` — text — `morning`: What to do in the morning
      - `midday` — text — `midday`: Where and what to eat at midday
      - `afternoon` — text — `afternoon`: What to do in the afternoon
      - `evening` — text — `evening`: What to do in the evening
  - `/result/costs` — list of structure trip_planner.CostLine — `costs`: The estimated cost, by category
    - each item is a structure trip_planner.CostLine (One line of the estimated cost), with these members (paths relative to one item, for DataTable columns or $item):
      - `category` — choice of "stay" | "food" | "tickets" | "transport" | "buffer" — `category`: What the money goes on
      - `amount` — number — `amount`: The estimated amount, in the trip's currency
  - `/result/estimated_total` — number — `estimated_total`: The estimated total cost of the trip
  - `/result/currency` — text — `currency`: The currency of every amount
  - `/result/practical_notes` — list of text — `practical_notes`: Notes for getting around and staying comfortable
    - each item is a text

## Delegated

None. `MthdsResult` remains available for any structure you choose not to lay out.

## One real run, as loaded

The state of one actual run, so you can judge magnitudes and lengths. Bind to the paths; do not copy these values into the spec.
